page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-24 is a network-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for compute-heavy workloads requiring dedicated processing power. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, the instance provides 24 dedicated virtual central processing units paired with 48 GB of system memory, establishing a compute-dense ratio of 2 GB of memory per vCPU core.

The hardware configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed through network-attached block storage volumes. Accelerators are omitted entirely, with zero physical or virtual GPUs provisioned on the host. In addition, the instance includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating either secondary network addressing or NAT gateways for external internet egress.

From an architectural standpoint, allocating 2 GB per core aligns the server with high-throughput compute tasks rather than memory-heavy or caching footprints. While benchmark metrics are unavailable for this profile, dedicated vCPU scheduling ensures predictable execution by isolating execution threads from multi-tenant CPU oversubscription. Deployments requiring local scratch disks must balance network block storage latency tradeoffs against CPU processing speeds.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to its lean resource allocation, maximizing dedicated compute density without carrying the overhead costs of attached local NVMe drives, auxiliary GPUs, or excess memory. Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-24 is best suited for compute-bound network applications, distributed microservices, CI/CD code compilation, media transcode pipelines, and batch computing tasks.
